clue.text: Contribution that, on reflection, sounds of little value?

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
tells us the letters are those heard when the word is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: tuppenny, worth two old pennies, means cheap or of little worth; said aloud it is 'tup-nee'

explanation.surface: A remark at a meeting that, thinking it over, seems pretty worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: TUPPENNY (worth two old British pennies) is pronounced roughly TUP-NI; 'on reflection' turns those letters round. 'sounds' looks like a verb about noise but signals the pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something put in to a discussion or project is one's contribution.

clue.text: Friend suppresses unconscious thought to become bully

indicators.note: to suppress is to keep something held down inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: a close friend is an intimate
the id, the unconscious part of the mind in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: A pal stifles a hidden urge and turns into a tormentor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bully someone is to frighten them into submission.

clue.text: One added to letter, and one more letter

indicators.note: the first piece is attached after the second

parts.note: PS, a postscript added to a letter
I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Adding a postscript and then one more note to a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' gives PS by association: a postscript is what one adds to a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the twenty-third letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Singer, singer, singer?

parts.note: one singer written three times over is threefold, and a boy soprano is also called by this word

explanation.walkthrough: The word means threefold, as the triple repeat shows, and is also the name for a high boy's voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano is this kind of singer, and the word also means threefold.

clue.text: Citizen of Europe, beefcake

definitions.meaning: a native of Hamburg, the German port city
read literally, a cake or patty of minced beef

explanation.surface: Describes a handsome muscular European man.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of Hamburg takes the city's name, and a minced-beef patty is a cake of beef.

clue.text: All of us smell half rancid, surprisingly excellent!

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something turned out unexpectedly, so these letters are rearranged
takes the first half, three of the six letters, of rancid

parts.note: ace means excellent

explanation.surface: Everyone stinks of rotten food, yet unexpectedly it is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes RAN from RANCID and 'surprisingly' rearranges it to ANR. HUM is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole of mankind includes every one of us.

clue.text: Fruit, piece with zest

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
energy and drive, go

explanation.surface: A slice of fruit with some grated peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tropical stone fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Cook too little grub, primarily, for the unlikely winner

parts.note: to undercook is to underdo

indicators.note: takes just the first letter of grub

explanation.surface: Serving undercooked food to someone not expected to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the competitor expected to lose who may yet triumph.

clue.text: Journalists often lying -— by the roadside?

definitions.meaning: sensationalist tabloid newspapers and their reporters
read literally, something pressed into the channel at the edge of a road

explanation.definitionFit: Tabloids with a reputation for invention are called this, and literally it is something pressed into a drain at the kerb.

clue.text: Cause to support

definitions.meaning: the origin or source of something
to cheer on, as in ... for a team

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the source of a problem and, as a verb, to cheer for a side.

clue.text: Family member merits ban when misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving letters are out of order, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative who deserves to be barred for bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a member of a tribe belongs to a large kinship group, a family in the broad sense.

clue.text: Simple song finally changed? It's the same again

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A repetitive tune whose ending is altered, yet still sounds identical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally changed' swaps the last letter Y of DITTY for an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is the word, and mark, used to say something repeats what came before.

clue.text: US president after relations initially with mainly dizzy actress

indicators.note: the anagram stands after the president's name in the clue but comes before it in the answer
a dizzy head spins, so these letters are whirled into a new order
takes just the opening letter of the word relations

parts.note: James Monroe, fifth president of the United States

explanation.surface: Hints at a scatterbrained Hollywood star linked romantically with an American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dizzy' is the anagram signal, working on the first letter of 'relations' plus the word mainly; 'after' sets the president's surname last even though the clue mentions him first.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American film star of the 1950s, famed for comic and glamorous roles.

clue.text: Looking at her case after a review, call for protection?

indicators.note: a ring encloses and protects what lies within it, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: a review reworks material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer investigating her file after a fresh look, asking for police protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a review' signals the anagram of 'her case'; 'for protection' has the word for call wrap round it, the way a protective ring encloses something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: studying or investigating a subject closely.

clue.text: Modest dwelling — evidently not music to grandad's ears?

definitions.meaning: a small self-contained apartment attached to a family home

definitions.text: evidently not music to grandad's ears?
definitions.meaning: read literally, grandmother singing out of tune

explanation.definitionFit: A small annexe for an elderly relative is called this, and literally it is a grandmother off-key.

clue.text: Lovely plate

definitions.meaning: as a noun, an attractive person
a shallow vessel food is served on

explanation.definitionFit: Informally an attractive person is called this, and it is also a serving vessel for food.

clue.text: One buying nibbles with a tiny crustacean

indicators.note: something that nibbles takes a bit into its mouth, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a person making a purchase is a shopper
with means and, joining things together

explanation.surface: A customer snacking alongside a little shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nibbles' is a container signal: the buyer takes the joining word into its mouth, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the small jumping amphipod found on beaches, also called a beach flea.

clue.text: A little wind, as duvet slid off

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A light breeze as the bedcover slipped to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small whirlwind that lifts dust and sand into a spinning column.

clue.text: Lamb, perhaps? Son, for example, is partial to regular slices of meat

indicators.note: the regular letters of meat take in the other pieces, enclosing them
takes every other letter of meat

parts.note: S, the abbreviation for son
say, as in 'take, say, a dog'

explanation.surface: A boy, for instance, likes evenly cut slices of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular slices of' takes alternate letters of meat, and 'partial to' has them hold the rest. Charles Lamb was an English essayist; 'Lamb' tempts as the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia, so he was a writer of short prose pieces.

clue.text: Definition thus ends in "cross" — does it?

definitions.text: Definition thus ends in "cross" — does it?

parts.words: Definition thus ends in "cross" — does it?
parts.note: the clue talks about itself: a clue's definition sits at one end, and here the word cross is printed at the end, so the answer is a word meaning cross

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a clue's definition really finishes on the word cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a word meaning lying across, so 'cross' at the end of the clue really is its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: transverse means crosswise, lying or extending across something.

clue.text: Average — or low?

definitions.meaning: the arithmetic average of a set of numbers

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a statistical average and also describes a stingy or base person.

clue.text: Spirited king close to one month on

indicators.note: only the closing part of the month's name is kept, its start dropped

parts.note: October, one month of the year

explanation.surface: A lively monarch nearly a month older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' drops OCT from OCTOBER, leaving OBER; ON is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the king of the fairies, spirits, in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Church welcomes acclaimed leader of sinfonia in diligent French musician

indicators.note: a host welcomes a guest inside, so the second word goes into the first

parts.note: CE, the Church of England
praised highly, lauded

indicators.note: the first letter is placed inside the word for diligent

parts.note: hard-working and occupied, busy

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of sinfonia

explanation.surface: A church honours a renowned conductor of a sinfonia within a hard-working French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' and 'in' are both container signals; CE is the standard abbreviation for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French composer of La Mer and Clair de Lune.

clue.text: Daughter raised in a country residence in Russia

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a letter lifts it to the top

parts.note: Chad, a country in central Africa
D, the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl brought up abroad in a Russian country house.
explanation.walkthrough: A followed by CHAD has its D 'raised' to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Russian country house or summer villa.

clue.text: Success lassoing a wagon

indicators.note: a lasso loops around its catch, so the first word encloses the a

parts.note: a victory, a win

explanation.surface: A cowboy triumphs by roping a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: a farm wagon or cart.

clue.text: Party in jail, no end in sight — what might have helped?

indicators.note: the party goes inside what remains of jail
neither end of the word jail is left showing, only its middle letters

parts.note: LIB, short for the Liberal party

explanation.surface: A celebration behind bars with no release date, and a question about what could have kept someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end in sight' means neither end of jail shows, leaving its middle pair; 'in' puts the party inside. LIB is the usual short form of Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof of being elsewhere at the time of a crime is what might have helped someone avoid prison.

clue.text: Model put on outfit the wrong way, underclothes essentially on the outside?

indicators.note: the middle letters of the garment word sit around the other pieces
takes the central letters, the essence, of underclothes

parts.note: on, as in placed on top of, means over

indicators.note: the word for outfit is read backwards

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothing or equipment

explanation.surface: A fashion model dresses back to front, with her underwear showing on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the middle pair of underclothes; 'the wrong way' turns the outfit word round; 'on the outside' wraps the middle pair round the rest. 'put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fashion model whose photograph appears on a magazine's front page.

clue.text: Top European hotel

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a Finn, a native of Finland

explanation.surface: Praising the best hotel in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb here, removing the first letter: FINN loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pub or small hotel offering lodging.

clue.text: End of day approaching, unlikely hosts beginning to fade

parts.note: near, nigh

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the first letter of fade goes inside

parts.note: tall, as in a tall story that is hard to believe

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word fade

explanation.surface: Evening draws near, as improbable hosts start to wane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' puts F ('beginning to fade') inside TALL; a tall story is an unlikely one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the onset of darkness at dusk marks the close of the day.

clue.text: Piece of music I found in books

indicators.note: the word for I is placed inside the abbreviation for books

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
